bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Plans State Maritime and Waterways Master Plan - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Plans State Maritime and Waterways Master Plan 27 Nov 2026 3 min read Why in News? The Bihar Transport Department is preparing a State Maritime and Waterways Master Plan to explore the commercial use of the state's rivers for cargo transportation and passenger services. Key Points: Objective of the Master Plan: The initiative aims to assess the transport potential of Bihar's river network and identify suitable waterways for commercial navigation. Identify rivers and stretches suitable for cargo transportation. Explore the feasibility of passenger transport through inland waterways. Determine infrastructure requirements, investment needs and development priorities. Consultant Selection Process: The Transport Department has invited proposals from agencies for preparing the master plan. The proposal submission deadline is 8 December 2026 . The selected consultant will assess the geographical conditions, navigability and transport capacity of rivers. Potential Benefits: Cargo Movement: Rivers could provide an alternative for transporting bulk goods and other commercial cargo. Passenger Connectivity: Inland waterways may provide additional travel options for people living along riverbanks. Reduced Road Congestion: Shifting some freight movement to waterways could reduce pressure from heavy vehicles on roads. Lower Logistics Costs: Water transport can be economical for suitable bulk cargo over navigable routes. Regional Development: Development of terminals, jetties and associated facilities could support local economic activities and employment. Important Rivers and Existing National Waterways in Bihar: Ganga River – National Waterway 1 (NW-1): An important inland water transport corridor passing through Bihar. Permanent terminals have been developed at Patna and Kalughat. Floating terminals or jetties have been established at Bhagalpur, Manihari (Katihar) and Buxar. Gandak River – National Waterway 37 (NW-37): Two community jetties have been deployed at Mangalpur (Nautan) and opposite bank in Bettiah. A Detailed Project Report (DPR) is being updated to assess its cargo and passenger transport potential. Kosi River – National Waterway 58 (NW-58): The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) conducted a hydrographic survey in 2024. The river was not found feasible for cargo movement based on that survey. National Framework for Inland Waterways: The National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 inland waterways as National Waterways. Their combined length is approximately 20,187 km , spread across 23 States and four Union Territories. The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), established under the IWAI Act, 1985, is responsible for the development and regulation of inland waterways for shipping and navigation. The Inland Vessels Act, 2021 provides a uniform framework for vessel registration, safety, survey, navigation and pollution prevention. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar establishes 5 regional language centres to promote Maithili, Bhojpuri, Magahi and ...
bihar_raw_news.content: India's Best Colleges 2026 Home News Bihar establishes 5 regional language centres to promote Maithili, Bhojpuri, Magahi and other languages ADVERTISEMENT Bihar establishes 5 regional language centres to promote Maithili, Bhojpuri, Magahi and other languages Bihar has selected five DIETs to promote Maithili, Magahi, Bhojpuri, Angika and Bajjika through teacher training, learning materials, cultural activities and research, in line with NEP 2020. Curated by Yash Wardhan Singh Image: iStock Nov 27, 2026 Share The Bihar government has selected five District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs) to work as centres for promoting regional languages. These centres will focus on Maithili, Magahi, Bhojpuri, Angika and Bajjika. The five centres will be set up at DIETs in Darbhanga, Gaya, Saran, Bhagalpur and Muzaffarpur. Each centre will work on one of these languages, as reported by PTI. The initiative has been approved by Bihar Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari and will be carried out through the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT). Officials said the programme has been planned in accordance with the National Education Policy 2020. The centres will prepare teaching and learning materials for each language. They will also conduct teacher training sessions and workshops, record regional languages and folk literature, and encourage research on teaching in students' mother tongues and how it affects their learning. According to the report, each centre will have a five-member committee. It will include a nodal officer, a language expert and three other members. The invited members may include teachers, writers, academicians and folk artists. These committees will prepare resource libraries, publish journals and organise literary and cultural programmes, officials told PTI. The initiative is expected to make classroom teaching easier for children to understand, improve their language skills and help preserve Bihar's cultural heritage. As per a notification issued by the Bihar Education Department, the selected committees have been asked to submit their reports to SCERT within 10 days. Meanwhile, Education Department Additional Chief Secretary C K Anil issued an order last week asking schools not to call teachers for meetings, training sessions, video conferences or workshops during school hours. bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar Extends 500 MWh Standalone BESS Tender For Seventh Time The tender seeks to appoint a Battery Energy Storage System Developer (BESSD) for setting up a 125 MW/500 MWh standalone storage project at Kajra. The project will have a four-hour storage duration. Vidushi Saxena 27 Nov 2026 13:55 IST Follow Us The Bihar State Power Generation Company Limited (BSPGCL) has extended the bidding deadline for its 500 MWh standalone Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project at Kajra in Lakhisarai district for the seventh time. The latest extension notice moves the online bid submission deadline from November 27 to December 11. Advertisment Under the revised schedule, bidders can submit their online bids until December 11, 2026, at 4 PM. The deadline for submission of physical documents has also been extended to December 11 at 4 PM, while the bids are scheduled to open at 5 PM on the same day. Advertisment The tender seeks to appoint a Battery Energy Storage System Developer (BESSD) for setting up a 125 MW/500 MWh standalone storage project at Kajra. The project will have a four-hour storage duration. Why Has BSPGCL Extended The BESS Tender Again? The latest notice marks the seventh extension to the tender timeline since its initial release. BSPGCL had previously issued extension notices on September 23, October 12, October 26, October 29, November 6 and November 12. Advertisment The previous extension had moved the bid submission deadline to November 27. The latest revision provides another 14 days for prospective bidders to complete the submission process. How Will The 500 MWh BESS Project Be Developed? The project will be implemented under the Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) framework on a Build, Own, Operate and Transfer (BOOT) basis. BSPGCL will provide the land for the proposed storage facility . Advertisment The selected developer will be responsible for setting up the standalone BESS project in accordance with the tender conditions. The procurement is intended to add four-hour battery storage capacity to Bihar's power infrastructure. bihar_raw_news.title: 11 doctors face dismissal over prolonged unauthorised absence in Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: 11 doctors face dismissal over prolonged unauthorised absence in Bihar Subscribe to Notifications Written By : Rumela De Sarkar Published On 2026-11-27 08:11 GMT | Update On 2026-11-27 08:11 GMT Patna: In a move to enforce discipline and accountability in the state healthcare system, the Bihar government has approved the dismissal of 11 doctors who allegedly remained absent from duty for prolonged periods without authorisation. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday. The doctors were posted at government healthcare facilities in Saharsa, Bhagalpur, Supaul, Banka and Madhepura. Their prolonged absence had reportedly affected the functioning of healthcare services. Also Read:Jharkhand initiates process to terminate 631 doctors over prolonged absence Explaining the decision, Nishant Kumar said the medical profession was not merely a job but a commitment to serving humanity. He said prolonged absence from duty and failure to fulfil professional responsibilities constituted a serious matter. The minister said the government had to take action against the concerned doctors in accordance with the rules. He also urged doctors and other healthcare workers across Bihar to perform their duties with complete honesty and responsibility, reports India Today . The action has been taken under the provisions of the Bihar Government Servants (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 2005. Rule 14(xi) provides for disciplinary action in cases involving unauthorised absence from duty, reports Patna Press . According to the news reports, the doctors facing dismissal were posted at the following government health facilities: • Sadar Hospital, Saharsa • Sadar Hospital, Bhagalpur • Community Health Centre (CHC), Pipra, Supaul • Sadar Hospital, Bhagalpur • Additional Primary Health Centre (APHC), Mamlakha, Sabour, Bhagalpur • Primary Health Centre (PHC), Marauna, Supaul • CHC Pipra, Supaul • APHC Sajour, Shahkund, Bhagalpur • APHC Golhatti, Bounsi, Banka • Sadar Hospital, Madhepura Although the Cabinet has approved the dismissal of 11 doctors, the available details identify only 10 doctors and their respective postings. Information about the remaining doctor was not available. As per official details, the doctors had remained absent from their respective postings for extended periods, with cases of unauthorised absence dating back to 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2021. The concerned departments initiated disciplinary proceedings against the doctors and subsequently forwarded the dismissal proposals to the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC), Patna. The Commission reportedly granted its consent in October 2026. After completion of the departmental proceedings and receipt of the Commission's approval, the proposals were placed before the state Cabinet for consideration. With the Cabinet's approval, the government has cleared the way for their dismissal under the applicable service rules. The decision is part of the Bihar government's efforts to strengthen accountability and ensure discipline among government employees, particularly those responsible for delivering essential public services. Doctors appointed to government hospitals and health centres are expected to maintain regular attendance and ensure uninterrupted medical services. bihar_raw_news.title: Over Four Lakh Bank Loan Recovery Cases Pending in Bihar Courts, Rs 5,623 Crore ...
bihar_raw_news.content: SHARE Prefer The420 on Google Stay ahead with our breaking stories and exclusive coverage prioritized on Google. Add The420 on Google → Muzaffarpur: Recovery of loans disbursed to the general public and farmers in Bihar has become a major challenge as 4,22,717 certificate cases remain pending in various executive and judicial courts across the state. Delays in hearing and resolving these cases have stalled the recovery of over Rs 5,623 crore for banks. Furthermore, in 1,668 cases where borrowers mortgaged plots of land, the process of taking possession of properties worth around Rs 561 crore is stuck due to pending court proceedings. The data emerged during a sub-committee meeting of the State Level Bankers’ Committee held on the 12th of this month. According to the information presented at the meeting, the SARFAESI Act, which was enacted to facilitate debt recovery, is proving ineffective on the ground. The prolonged legal delays are placing an unnecessary burden on bank managements and pushing up their non-performing assets (NPAs), which directly restricts their capacity to issue fresh loans and slows down the rural economy. Muzaffarpur Tops in Pending Cases, Bhagalpur in Stuck Amount District-wise figures presented at the meeting show that Muzaffarpur leads the state in the number of pending loan recovery cases, with 27,361 cases awaiting resolution. The total amount stuck in these cases in Muzaffarpur stands at Rs 311 crore. Bhagalpur ranks second in terms of case volume with 27,181 pending matters, followed by Banka at third with 23,518 cases. East Champaran and West Champaran hold the fourth and fifth positions with 23,318 and 19,972 pending cases, respectively. When measured by the total amount of money locked in litigation, Bhagalpur faces the most severe situation in the state. The district has Rs 359 crore stuck across its pending recovery cases, placing it at the top of the list. Muzaffarpur is second with Rs 311 crore, while Banka stands third with Rs 306 crore awaiting recovery. East Champaran follows in fourth place with Rs 280 crore stuck, and West Champaran is fifth with Rs 207 crore locked in pending cases. Rural and Cooperative Banks Face Worst NPA Crisis The failure to recover overdue loans has pushed the overall state-level NPA of banks to 6.88 percent of total advances. Among the different banking categories, rural and cooperative banks are facing the sharpest deterioration in asset quality. The NPA level of rural banks has climbed to 18.85 percent, while cooperative banks have recorded an NPA of 17.41 percent. In comparison, nationalised public sector banks have managed to keep their NPA levels comparatively lower at 6 percent. Private sector banks are in a relatively better position, with their NPA standing at 4.21 percent. The high NPA ratios in rural and cooperative institutions remain a serious concern because these banks play a primary role in meeting the credit requirements of farmers and rural borrowers. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Strengthens Energy Storage Readiness with Two-Day BESS Capacity-Building ... - Technuter
bihar_raw_news.content: November 27, 2026 technuter 4 min read The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI), under the Indo-German development cooperation project Energy Storage for Renewable Energy Integration in India (StoREin), organized a two-day capacity-building programme on Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) for Bihar’s power utilities officials on 25–26 November 2026 in Patna. The programme was organized in collaboration with Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH and in close cooperation with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). In a message shared on the occasion, the Hon’ble Energy Minister of Bihar highlighted the state’s focus on ensuring clean, affordable and reliable power to support its economic growth. The message stated: “After achieving universal electricity access in record time, Bihar’s next goal is to provide clean, affordable and reliable power for rapid economic growth. Along with Distributed Renewable Energy sources we are also focusing on Pumped Storage, Battery storage and Nuclear Energy to ensure availability of quality power in the state.” The programme aimed to strengthen the technical and operational understanding of officials from Bihar’s power-sector institutions and support the effective planning, development and utilization of battery energy storage systems. It brought together 80+ participants from key institutions, including the Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency (BREDA), Bihar State Power Holding Company Limited (BSPHCL), Bihar State Power Generation Company Limited (BSPGCL), Bihar State Power Transmission Company Limited (BSPTCL), North Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited (NBPDCL) and South Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited (SBPDCL), along with experts and representatives from the energy sector. Why storage, why Bihar, why now The Bihar Renewable Energy Policy, 2025 targets 24 GW of renewable energy capacity and 6.1 GWh of energy storage by 2030. Bihar recorded a peak demand of 9,475 MW at 9:50 pm on 16 July 2026, when solar power was unavailable. BESS can help meet such evening peaks reliably while reducing costly power procurement, supporting renewable energy integration and deferring network investments. Delivering the keynote address, Shri Ajay Yadav, IAS, CMD, BSPHCL and Secretary, Energy Department, Government of Bihar , highlighted the importance of energy storage in meeting the state’s growing electricity demand while ensuring affordable power supply. He noted that Bihar’s demand could reach around 11,000 MW in the coming years and that managing peak demand and the cost of power procurement would remain important considerations. He also highlighted the comparatively shorter installation timelines of container-based BESS, which can be deployed in 12–15 months, compared with pumped storage projects that may take five to six years to construct. In his welcome address, Shri Alekhya Datta, Director, Electricity and Renewables Division, TERI , emphasised the need for a coordinated and evidence-based approach to storage planning in Bihar. He highlighted the importance of identifying suitable locations and applications for BESS based on hourly demand patterns, renewable energy availability and network constraints. He also underlined the potential of smart-meter data in informing these decisions and stressed that storage procurement should be guided by the services required by the power system rather than driven solely by capacity targets

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar plans pharma park to attract major drug firms: Minister
bihar_raw_news.content: Policy & Regulations 1 min Read Bihar plans pharma park to attract major drug firms: Minister Addressing a national-level programme organised by the Govt Pharmacy Institute to mark World Pharmacists Day and National Pharmacy Week 2026, Jaiswal said the proposed policy would facilitate the setting up of pharmaceutical manufacturing units in Bihar and promote local production of medicines. Jai Narain Pandey TNN Published On Nov 27, 2026 at 11:10 AM IST Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Patna: Bihar will set up a pharma park and bring out a new policy to attract major domestic and international pharmaceutical companies to invest in the state, revenue and land reforms minister Dilip Kumar Jaiswal said on Wednesday. Addressing a national-level programme organised by the Govt Pharmacy Institute to mark World Pharmacists Day and National Pharmacy Week 2026, Jaiswal said the proposed policy would facilitate the setting up of pharmaceutical manufacturing units in Bihar and promote local production of medicines. Highlighting the expansion of drug regulatory infrastructure, Jaiswal said Rs 57 crore had been allocated, with central govt support, to develop drug offices in all 38 districts and the State Drug Controller's office. Construction has been completed in 19 districts. He said Bihar currently has 124 drug inspectors against 163 sanctioned posts. The govt is considering issuing a recruitment notification to fill the remaining 39 vacancies. Expressing concern over the indiscriminate use of antibiotics, Jaiswal said antimicrobial resistance (AMR) had emerged as a serious global health challenge. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on the issue in his 'Mann Ki Baat' programme, he said AMR could cause 10 million deaths annually worldwide by 2050. He stressed the need to discourage self-medication and ensure that medicines are taken only on medical advice. Jaiswal also formally launched 'Anveshan-2027', a national-level initiative in Bihar. He said the govt would provide incentives and facilities to pharmaceutical companies to attract investment and boost local medicine production. Comments What are your thoughts?

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar focuses on AI-driven healthcare, smart ambulances and real-time bed tracking
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar focuses on AI-driven healthcare, smart ambulances and real-time bed tracking Written By : Divyani Paul Published On 2026-11-27T11:04:34+05:30 | Updated On 27 Nov 2026 11:04 AM IST Patna- Artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to strengthen Bihar's healthcare system, with areas ranging from diagnostics and telemedicine to smart ambulances and real-time information on hospital bed availability, Health Minister Nishant Kumar said on Wednesday. He made remarks while inaugurating the 'AI for Healthier Bihar' workshop in Patna. The minister also noted that AI could improve the quality of and access to healthcare services, particularly in rural areas, where reaching specialist doctors remains a challenge. Also Read: Bihar plans 31 new medical colleges, aims to double MBBS seats to 10K by 2030 The workshop was organised to foster collaboration between the health department, technical institutions, and innovators. Attendees included Archana Vyas, Country Director of the Gates Foundation, and Dr Vasant Kumar, Director (Health), among others. According to the TOI report, 25 innovators showcased AI-based technologies at this workshop, aimed at addressing challenges within the state's healthcare system. Nishant stated that AI-based systems can help in identifying high-risk pregnant women, monitoring fetal health, predicting the spread of infectious diseases, and facilitating the early detection of cancer and other serious illnesses. He also stated that AI can assist in the analysis of CT scans, MRIs, ultrasounds, and X-ray reports for the early detection of diseases such as TB (tuberculosis) and cancer. The Minister also called for the expansion of AI-enabled telemedicine services and for making real-time information regarding bed availability in general wards, ICUs, HDUs, and CCUs accessible via a digital platform. He proposed launching a pilot project for smart ambulances, equipped with digital ECG machines, pulse oximeters, blood pressure monitors, GPS tracking, and digital connectivity with hospitals. Health Department Secretary Kumar Ravi and other senior officials visited the stalls to learn about their practical applications. Kumar Ravi stated that the workshop provided an opportunity to discuss challenges in medical education, nursing, and patient care, including issues such as the availability of specialists and super-specialists, as well as the analysis of data related to nursing. bihar_raw_news.content: Partnerships and Collaborations 1 min Read CIMP Patna, Kyonggi University sign MoU to promote AI research and student exchange Chandragupt Institute of Management Patna has signed an MoU with South Korea's Kyonggi University to explore AI applications in agriculture, tourism and urban development. The partnership will promote joint research, student exchanges, internships and faculty development programmes. TOI.in Published On Nov 27, 2026 at 11:53 AM IST Set ETEducation as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment CIMP Patna, Kyonggi University sign MoU to promote AI research and student exchange Patna: Chandragupt Institute of Management Patna (CIMP) has signed a memorandum of understanding with South Korea’s Kyonggi University to explore the use of artificial intelligence and other technologies can improve farming, urban planning and tourism in Bihar. Kyonggi University vice-president for special affairs Kiyoung Kim and CIMP chief administrative officer Kumod Kumar signed the memorandum of understanding in South Korea. The pact sets out four areas of cooperation under the Korea–Bihar AI Future Generation Programme: tourism, urban development, agriculture and smart farming . Under the pact, the two institutions will pursue joint research, student and faculty exchanges, internships and workshops. Plans also include joint publications and faculty development programmes. Students could work on projects involving AI, sustainable tourism and smart farming, while faculty members would have opportunities to collaborate on research and teaching. Kumar said the partnership would help Bihar access South Korean expertise in technology and AI, with a focus on adapting global practices to local needs, creating jobs and supporting economic growth. Kim said the Suwon-based university would contribute its experience in education and technology and help expand learning opportunities for young people. CIMP director Rana Singh said the institute aims to use the partnership to strengthen Bihar’s institutions and attract investment. Comments What are your thoughts?

bihar_raw_news.content: Governance 1 min Read Bihar CM says Constitution strengthens democratic traditions, inspires national unity "Our Constitution, based on the fundamental ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, is not merely the foundation of the country's system of governance, but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity," Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said. PTI Published On Nov 26, 2026 at 11:32 PM IST Set ETGovernment as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday urged people to uphold the core values of the Constitution , including justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, saying it is not merely the foundation of the country's governance system but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity. On the occasion of Constitution Day , he led a padayatra covering around 2 km in Bettiah town of West Champaran district - from Sagar Pokhra to Raj Deorhi. NDA workers and supporters from surrounding assembly constituencies also took part in the procession. Choudhary addressed party workers at Raj Deorhi, highlighting the importance of constitutional values, democratic institutions and national unity . Earlier in the day, in a post on X on the occasion of Constitution Day, he said the Constitution strengthens India's democratic traditions and inspires the nation to preserve its unity and integrity. "Our Constitution, based on the fundamental ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, is not merely the foundation of the country's system of governance, but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity," the CM said. "It inspires us to uphold the country's unity and integrity while strengthening our democratic traditions. On the occasion of Constitution Day, let us all resolve to embrace the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution in our lives, remain committed to democratic values, and further strengthen the spirit of fraternity and national unity," he added. India observes Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Diwas , every year on November 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) , chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL), Tamil Nadu , on 25 November 2026. Key Points: Project Overview: The project involves developing a 900-metre-long second container terminal at Kamarajar Port. Annual container-handling capacity: 2 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs) . It will be developed in two phases: Phase I: Capacity of 1.1 million TEUs. Phase II: Capacity of 0.9 million TEUs. Press Information Bureau Implementation Model – DBFOT: The project will follow the Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) model. The private concessionaire will design, construct, finance and operate the terminal. The concession period will be 40 years , including a construction period of 48 months. Capacity to Handle Large Container Vessels: The new terminal is designed to accommodate large mainline container ships. It will be capable of handling vessels of up to 24,346 TEUs and 400 metres in length. The 18-metre design draft will enable larger vessels to access the terminal. Existing Performance of Kamarajar Port: Handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY 2025–26. Container traffic exceeded 7 lakh TEUs during the same period. Existing container terminal capacity: 0.8 million TEUs annually. Actual container handling: approximately 0.7 million TEUs, representing around 88% capacity utilisation . Container traffic at Kamarajar Port grew at approximately 9.9% CAGR over the preceding five years, compared with around 7% growth nationally. Alignment with National Maritime Initiatives: Maritime India Vision 2030: Aims to enhance port infrastructure, maritime trade and logistics efficiency. Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047: Provides a long-term framework for developing India's maritime sector. Atmanirbhar Bharat: The project will strengthen domestic port capacity and reduce dependence on foreign transshipment infrastructure. About Kamarajar Port Limited: Formerly known as Ennore Port Limited . Located on the eastern coast of Tamil Nadu, near the Chennai industrial region. It is wholly owned by Chennai Port Authority under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. It handles coal, petroleum products, LNG, LPG, containers, automobiles and general cargo. During FY 2025–26, it recorded revenue of approximately ₹1,280 crore and profit before tax of ₹924 crore. bihar_raw_news.title: Delhi- Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Delhi-Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes Breaking News Delhi-Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes By Ananya Sharma November 27, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Delhi and Bihar are set to introduce year-round interstate bus services on 18 routes, with around 200 AC and non-AC buses connecting the national capital with destinations across Bihar, Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Singh said on Thursday. The services are expected to benefit nearly 20 lakh people from Bihar and Purvanchal who live and work in Delhi, as well as other passengers travelling between the two states. The proposed network is being introduced under a reciprocal transport agreement between Delhi and Bihar. Officials said the services are likely to be inaugurated on Friday, although operating timings have not yet been finalised. Fares are expected to be around Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000 for sleeper and non-sleeper categories. The routes will connect Delhi with destinations including Araria, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Darbhanga, East Champaran, Gaya, Kishanganj, Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Nawada, Patna and Purnia. The report also refers to destinations in the Bhagalpur region. Singh said the agreement would provide more convenient and accessible travel, particularly during peak seasons when passengers face heavy rush and limited train-ticket availability. The services are also intended to ease overcrowding on existing bus connections during festivals and other periods of high demand. To expand interstate transport capacity, the Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses for interstate operations, officials said. A further 150 buses are expected to be deployed through the public-private partnership model. Officials described the planned services as an environment-friendly public-transport initiative that would strengthen connectivity between Delhi and Bihar. The final schedule, route-wise frequency and operational arrangements had not been announced in the report. national_raw_news.title: 45th India International Trade Fair to conclude in New Delhi today
national_raw_news.content: The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will conclude today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Organised annually by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, it is one of India’s leading multi-product trade exhibitions. The theme of the fair this year is Vikas aur Virasat. An Award Presentation Ceremony was held yesterday, recognising outstanding displays and presentations by participating states and exhibitors. In the States and Union Territories category, Tamil Nadu was honoured with the gold award, Kerala received the silver award, Madhya Pradesh bagged the bronze award, while Tripura received the commendation prize. In the Ministries and Government Departments category, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) received the Gold Medal, the Ministry of Railways received the Silver Medal, and the Ministry of Textiles received the Bronze Medal. During the awards ceremony, Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh were recognised as partner states, while Assam, Delhi, Jharkhand and West Bengal were acknowledged as focus states for IITF 2026. Talking to the media, ITPO Chairman Jawed Ashraf said that this year the fair witnessed a significant increase in footfall compared to last year. He also highlighted that exhibitors witnessed higher business this year compared to the previous edition.

national_raw_news.title: India presents vision and roadmap for hosting 2036 Olympics before IOC Future Host Commission
national_raw_news.content: India presented its “vision and proposed roadmap” for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games in an online interaction with the International Olympic Committee’s Future Host Commission yesterday. The 30-minute presentation was followed by a brief discussion with the Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic-led nine-member Future Host Commission. The presentation covered proposed host city Ahmedabad’s preparedness, including sports infrastructure and the support extended by the city, state, and central authorities to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). It also covered India’s experience in hosting major international sporting events, proposed venue development plans, and the long-term vision for delivering the Games. Germany, Hungary, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, South Africa and Türkiye are the other countries that are bidding for the 2036 Games. After the presentation, the IOC will conduct an “anonymous survey” to get a sense of the general public’s view on India’s bid. The survey is expected to be done in the third week of December and will have a bearing on the evaluation of India’s bid in March next year, following which the phase of Strategic Dialogue will start. During this phase, the interested countries will be expected to provide an initial response to the Future Host Questionnaire and core financial guarantees.

national_raw_news.content: The Lok Sabha has been reconvened from Monday, while the Rajya Sabha will resume its sitting from Wednesday to transact essential government business. The sittings of both the Houses, subject to exigencies of the Business, may conclude on the 3rd of December. There would be no Question Hour, Zero Hour, or Private Members’ Business during the sittings of both the Houses. The move follows a government’s proposal to convene a special sitting of both Houses. As per the Lok Sabha Bulletin, Speaker Om Birla has directed that the Lok Sabha, which was adjourned sine die on the 13th of August, 2026, will now sit at 11 AM on Monday. The Rajya Sabha Bulletin also stated that the Upper House, which was adjourned sine die on the 13th of August, has been reconvened by the Rajya Sabha Chairman, C. P. Radhakrishnan, to meet at 11 AM on Wednesday to transact essential government business. Earlier, the Government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the sittings of the lower house and Upper House on these dates to transact essential Government Business. The Monsoon Session has not been prorogued so far following the adjournment of both the Houses sine die on August 13.
